title.narrative: Capacity Building of Public Sector Civil Services Training In

description.narrative: "The overall objective of the grant is to revitalize and upgrade Pakistan’s civil service training by: strengthening capacity of the public sector training institutions; revising curricula; improving teaching methodology using case-method techniques; building staff capacity; and improving connectivity within and among training institutes. Bulk of the amount approved under the IDF Grant is set aside for the Pakistan Administration Staff College (PASC) to strengthen its training capacity. The broad set of activities that are intended to be carried out under the Grant include: * improving/ revising curricula of PASC and other training institutions; * preparation of case studies for the PASC in order to improve its training capacity; * training of core/ key faculty of PASC, who would then serve as trainers for senior civil servants of the country. The proposed training include sending a select group of , faculty for training at Harvard under the Mason Fellowship Program; and/ or short courses at various leading interntional institutions; and * facility upgrade of PASC and other training institutions Administrative Restructuring; based on the recenly issued report of the restructuring committee, the Federal Government Divisions will be stremlined in order to cope with the new world. Implementing a Crash Program in public sector management to seniro civil servants, joint and additional secretaries to create ""Reform Champions"". This group will lead the change effort form within the civil service. This is being planned with the help of the Kennedy School of Government and the first batch of civil servants is expected to begin their education program in the next few months. the entire program will be completed by the end of 2002. Deepening the skill based of entry-level civil servants through scholarship programs; this would involve sending 5 percent of the brightest civil servants from each cohort ofentering civil servants (about 15 to 20 persons) for Master's degree programs at world class universities. This is planned as an annual event and will continue as part of human resource development. Upgrading faculty and establishing joint-training programs with major universities, strenthening the Civil Service Training Inistiutes; the intent is to have a ""twinning"" relationship with a world class university or with selected individual faculty members to promote faculty exchange and curricula reform. This relationship will span at least five years and is designed to help convert the current institutes into a National Public Sector Management University which can provide world class education domestically. Prompting use of distance learning and internet resources."
